# Beyond Earth — Project Summary

*What did you develop?*

Beyond Earth is a space exploration and rocket-building simulator developed using Roblox Studio, inspired by Kerbal Space Program. Players can design and assemble their own rockets using modular components, including command pods, fuel tanks, engines, and boosters. The game features a Vehicle Assembly Building (VAB), a launch facility, realistic-inspired rocket physics, fuel management, flight controls, orbital mechanics, and a visual representation of Earth and the Moon.

*How does it address the challenge?*

Beyond Earth addresses the challenge of making space exploration and rocket engineering more accessible, interactive, and engaging. Through hands-on rocket construction and flight simulation, players can experiment with different spacecraft designs while learning fundamental concepts such as gravity, thrust, fuel consumption, and orbital motion. Its modular building system encourages creativity, experimentation, and problem-solving.

* Why is it important? *

Beyond Earth combines education, creativity, and entertainment in one accessible gaming experience. It introduces players to aerospace engineering and space science through interactive gameplay, potentially inspiring, greater interest in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics). Beyond Earth Version 0.1 establishes the foundation for future improvements, including more advanced spacecraft systems and expanded space exploration opportunities.
details:
Beyond Earth — Project Details

Beyond Earth is a space exploration and rocket-building simulator developed on Roblox. Inspired by Kerbal Space Program, the project allows players to design, construct, launch, and control their own spacecraft while exploring the principles of spaceflight.

How Does It Work?

Players begin in the Vehicle Assembly Building (VAB), where they construct rockets using modular components such as command pods, fuel tanks, engines, and boosters. Once assembled, their rockets are transferred to the Space Center launchpad. Players can then ignite their engines, control their spacecraft, manage fuel consumption, and monitor flight information, including altitude, speed, and orbital trajectories.

The game also features a simulated gravitational environment, an interactive orbital map, atmospheric transitions, and visual representations of Earth and the Moon. Mathematical simulations have also been developed to demonstrate Earth-to-Moon transfers and lunar landings.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Beyond Earth makes space science and aerospace engineering more engaging and accessible through interactive gameplay. It encourages creativity, critical thinking, problem-solving, and experimentation.

The project's intended impact is to inspire young people to develop an interest in space exploration and STEM education. By allowing players to experiment with spacecraft designs and flight mechanics, Beyond Earth introduces scientific concepts through practical and entertaining experiences.

Development Tools and Technology

Beyond Earth was developed primarily using Roblox Studio and Luau, Roblox's scripting language. The project uses Roblox's physics engine, graphical user interface tools, 3D modeling features, and scripting systems to create its environments and gameplay mechanics.

Development was carried out on a computer, with ChatGPT assisting in programming, debugging, planning, and technical problem-solving.

Creativity and Innovation

What makes Beyond Earth creative is its combination of modular spacecraft construction, physics-based flight, orbital mechanics, and space exploration within Roblox.

Its separate VAB and Space Center environments allow players to experience both the engineering and operational aspects of space missions. The project also combines realistic-inspired scientific calculations with accessible gameplay, creating a learning experience that remains entertaining.

Important Development Considerations

Throughout development, several factors were considered, including:

  • Accessibility: Making rocket construction and flight understandable for players.
  • Performance: Accounting for Roblox's physics and world-size limitations.
  • Realism: Incorporating gravitational calculations, thrust, fuel consumption, and orbital motion.
  • User experience: Creating intuitive controls, clear interfaces, and useful flight instruments.
  • Expandability: Designing the game so new spacecraft components and celestial destinations can be introduced in future updates.

Conclusion

Beyond Earth Version 0.1 establishes a foundation for an educational and creative space simulation experience. By combining programming, engineering concepts, and interactive game design, the project demonstrates how Roblox can be used for both entertainment and STEM-inspired learning.
